content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To learn how to speak italian, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Memorize 100 common Italian verbs (3 days)
Step 2. Write a short essay about your family in Italian (4 hours)
Step 3. Enroll in a beginner Italian online course (1 hour)
Step 4. Attend a weekend immersion workshop (2 days)
Step 5. Pass a level A1 proficiency quiz (1 hour)
Step 6. Practice pronunciation of double consonants (2 hours)
Step 7. Buy a comprehensive Italian-English dictionary (30 minutes)
Step 8. Learn the rules for definite and indefinite articles (4 hours)
Step 9. Study the difference between "essere" and "stare" (2 hours)
Step 10. Master the use of the "passato prossimo" tense (1 week)
Step 11. Learn how to order food at a restaurant (1 hour)
Step 12. Practice basic greetings and introductions (2 hours)
Step 13. Download a language learning app (10 minutes)
Step 14. Watch an Italian film with Italian subtitles (2 hours)
Step 15. Listen to an Italian language podcast (30 minutes)
Step 16. Label household items with their Italian names (1 hour)
Step 17. Learn the Italian alphabet and phonics (2 hours)
Step 18. Study the conjugation of irregular verbs (5 days)
Step 19. Have a 15-minute conversation with a native speaker (15 minutes)
Step 20. Learn how to tell time in Italian (1 hour)
Step 21. Practice counting from one to one hundred (1 hour)
Step 22. Learn common Italian idioms and expressions (3 hours)
Step 23. Research Italian culture and etiquette (2 hours)
Step 24. Study the use of prepositions (4 hours)
Step 25. Learn the names of common fruits and vegetables (1 hour)
Step 26. Practice using "c'è" and "ci sono" (1 hour)
Step 27. Learn how to ask for directions (2 hours)
Step 28. Study the "imperfetto" tense (4 days)
Step 29. Set your phone's language to Italian (5 minutes)
Step 30. Listen to Italian opera and translate the lyrics (3 hours)
Step 31. Learn how to describe people's physical appearance (2 hours)
Step 32. Review the rules for noun-adjective agreement (3 hours)
Step 33. Write a letter to an Italian pen pal (1 hour)
Step 34. Find a list of the 500 most used Italian words (20 minutes)
Step 35. Practice ordering a coffee at an Italian bar (30 minutes)
Step 36. Read a children's book in Italian (2 hours)
Step 37. Browse Italian language learning blogs (1 hour)
Step 38. Learn the names of the days of the week and months (1 hour)
Step 39. Choose an Italian city to focus your dialect study on (30 minutes)
Step 40. Watch a YouTube tutorial on Italian hand gestures (15 minutes)
Step 41. Learn how to express likes and dislikes (2 hours)
Step 42. Study the formation of plural nouns (2 hours)
Step 43. Learn the names of different body parts (1 hour)
Step 44. Take a formal Italian language exam (3 hours)
Step 45. Participate in an Italian conversation exchange (1 hour)
Step 46. Find an Italian radio station to stream (10 minutes)
Step 47. Learn the possessive adjectives (3 hours)
Step 48. Study reflexive verbs and pronouns (5 hours)
Step 49. Learn how to talk about the weather (1 hour)
Step 50. Watch an Italian news broadcast (30 minutes)
Step 51. Buy a set of Italian verb conjugation flashcards (15 minutes)
Step 52. Write a daily journal entry in Italian (45 minutes)
Step 53. Learn how to use "molto," "poco," and "troppo" (1 hour)
Step 54. Study the formal vs. informal "you" (2 hours)
Step 55. Learn Italian slang used by teenagers (2 hours)
Step 56. Research the history of the Italian language (3 hours)
Step 57. Practice tongue twisters to improve fluency (1 hour)
Step 58. Learn the names of various professions (2 hours)
Step 59. Create a study schedule for the month (30 minutes)
Step 60. Look up common Italian last names (10 minutes)
Step 61. Practice using "andare" and "venire" correctly (2 hours)
Step 62. Learn how to shop for clothes in Italian (1 hour)
Step 63. Sign up for a library card to borrow Italian books (15 minutes)
Step 64. Study the future tense (3 days)
Step 65. Learn how to make comparisons (2 hours)
Step 66. Practice identifying gender of nouns (2 hours)
Step 67. Buy an Italian cookbook (20 minutes)
Step 68. Learn how to use the word "ne" (4 hours)
Step 69. Translate a short news article into English (1 hour)
Step 70. Learn the names of different rooms in a house (1 hour)
